subject.title: Gateway should expose HTTP REST endpoints for common queries

question: Should trusted admin HTTP RPC expose read-only session query methods such as `sessions.list`, `sessions.get`, or `sessions.describe`, or should HTTP session-data access wait for a narrower session API design?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but exposing session data over HTTP is a Gateway operator/security boundary and public API shape decision that automation should not choose unilaterally.

options.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
options.body: Add only maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist, with docs and tests.

options.title: Use broader session API design
options.body: Keep this issue as context and let https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/20934 own a dedicated session HTTP API shape before exposing more session data.

options.title: Keep sessions WebSocket-only
options.body: Document that session list/detail remain available through Gateway WebSocket RPC and not through HTTP for now.

recommendation.title: Extend admin HTTP RPC
recommendation.body: Add only maintainer-approved read-only session query methods to the existing default-off trusted admin HTTP RPC allowlist, with docs and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the admin HTTP RPC and Gateway HTTP security boundary touched by this decision.
